attacks.claim: Dark mode breaks the day cards. .day-card hard-codes a white background, while the dark-mode block remaps --text to near-white, so card text is near-invisible for the roughly 30% of users on dark OS settings.
The visual QA pass covers only light mode (Chrome 1440px, iPhone 14). The dark-mode card defect is untested, and the 360-414px range that carries 68% of sessions has a single device run.
attacks.evidence: Visual QA vs Figma: Chrome 1440px (light), Safari iPhone 14 (light) — pass, pixel diffs < 1%.

attacks.claim: The 72px fixed action bar has no bottom clearance on .planner, so the Sunday card and its tile controls can sit under the bar at end of scroll. No safe-area inset is handled, and no scroll-to-end check is reported.
attacks.evidence: .action-bar { position: fixed; ... height: 72px; } with .planner { ... padding: 16px; } and "Sunday is the last child of .planner"

attacks.claim: The most frequent action (9.4 adds per WAU per week, 64% on mobile) moves from a one-tap tile button to a multi-step path through the recipe page and servings sheet. No before/after measurement or shortcut is given, and the artifact does not show the button is a clutter problem.
attacks.evidence: "The old tile-level '+ List' button is removed to declutter tiles." / "tap the tile → recipe page → 'Ingredients' tab → choose servings in the servings sheet → 'Add to list'"

attacks.claim: The rollout goes to 100% of web users in one step with no canary stage. The watch list names metrics but gives no thresholds, alert conditions or rollback trigger, so a regression is found only after full exposure.
attacks.evidence: "Ship to 100% Tue 10:00 PT behind planner_v7" / "Watch: planner page JS errors, shopping-list additions/WAU, planner bounce rate."

attacks.claim: 'Generate shopping list' adds all of the week's recipes in one tap. It has no stated dedupe against ingredients already added individually, and no undo, unlike the single-recipe flow.
attacks.evidence: "'Generate shopping list' (adds all planned recipes for the week)" vs "toast with 'Undo'" on the single-recipe add

attacks.claim: Each tile's Swap button has the same accessible name, so screen-reader users hear repeated 'Swap' with no recipe context. The overflow button is labelled, so this is a gap rather than a failure.
attacks.evidence: <button class="btn-ghost">Swap</button> vs aria-label="More options for Sheet-pan gnocchi"

attacks.claim: Touch drag-to-move on 360-414px screens is not described or tested, and it can conflict with vertical scroll. The QA cites no touch device.
attacks.evidence: "Drag a recipe tile between days to move it." / QA: "Drag-and-drop between days … pass"

attacks.claim: The artifact does not describe what 'Share plan' exposes, or its visibility, expiry, revocation or consent. The share surface cannot be assessed for personal-data exposure until this is specified.
attacks.evidence: ABSENT: scope, visibility, expiry, revocation or consent for "Share plan"

attacks.claim: Dark-mode surfaces disagree. The action bar uses --surface (#1c1c1e), cards are #ffffff and the page is #000, and the bar's rgba(0,0,0,.08) border is nearly invisible on dark.
attacks.evidence: .action-bar { background: var(--surface); border-top: 1px solid rgba(0,0,0,.08); } vs .day-card { background: #ffffff; }

attacks.claim: Colour is split between hard-coded hex and tokens. That split caused the dark-mode defect and will recur as the theme grows.
No dark-mode Figma frame is referenced, so the pixel-diff claim has no design source for the dark theme the CSS implements.
attacks.evidence: Figma: "Planner 7 final"; QA compares light mode only
